mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% over the past month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers a flight to quality and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which drives corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes, INDPRO declines do not produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past month indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months with PAYEMS growth above 100k.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the core consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months with CPIAUCSL above 2.0% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 1.0% per annum signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-cycle expansion regime, a quarterly growth rate in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.0% signals strong economic momentum, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In early-cycle expansion regimes, GDPC1 growth above 2.0% fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.
